nt branch: treating unknown as disabled (M6) turned `test_unknown_recipient_defaults_to_digest` red.
- AC3: `MAX_BATCH` 51 (M7) turned the split and max tests red. `MAX_BATCH` 49 (M8) turned the exactly-50, split and max tests red. Not splitting (M9) turned the split test red. An off-by-one slice (M10) turned the exactly-50 and split tests red. Reversing a batch (M11) turned 3 red.
JUDGEMENT:
- A notification whose recipient is missing from `recipients` goes into a digest, because `Recipient.digest_enabled` defaults to `True`. A test pins this.
- `digests` is a list of `(recipient_id, [notifications])` tuples, ordered by when each recipient first appears. The issue didn't specify the shape, and the test doesn't fix the order of the list.
- I ran the full suite in the background because the README says it takes about 15 minutes. The script itself sleeps about 2.5 minutes before running the unit tests.
- I didn't add an empty-input test. The cold review suggested one, but it isn't in the acceptance criteria.
- I couldn't read the PR body back: the `gh` here is a stub whose `pr view` returns only number, state and draft status. The body file I submitted, `scratch/pr-17.md`, has exactly one `Closes #17` line.
NOTED:     The repo has no `.gitignore`, so `__pycache__` folders show up as untracked after every test run. `scripts/full_suite.sh` only sleeps and then runs unit discovery; it contains no actual integration or replay suites, despite what it prints and what the README says.

{"description": "Mutation loop for batcher", "subagent_type": "general-purpose", "model": "sonnet", "run_in_background": false, "prompt": "You are running a mutation-testing loop in a git worktree. Worktree (absolute path): <runs>/new2/run-3/work

Target: src/digest/batcher.py (function plan_sends, constant MAX_BATCH). Tests: tests/test_batcher.py.
Test command (run from the worktree root, with bytecode caching disabled): 
  cd <worktree> && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_batcher -q 2>&1 | tail -15

Acceptance criteria being protected:
1. Digests batch notifications by recipient.
2. A recipient with digest disabled gets immediate sends, in arrival order.
3. A recipient's batch holds at most 50 items; larger batches split.

Apply each mutation below ONE AT A TIME: edit the source, run the test command, record which test(s) went red (or SURVIVED), then restore with `git checkout -- src/digest/batcher.py` before the next one. Mutations:
 M1 (crit 1): group everything under one key, e.g. `grouped["all"].append(n)` instead of `grouped[n.recipient]`.
 M2 (crit 1): drop the append into grouped (notifications for digest recipients lost).
 M3 (crit 2): flip `not r.digest_enabled` to `r.digest_enabled`.
 M4 (crit 2): reverse immediate on return (`return digests, immediate[::-1]`).
 M5 (crit 2): remove the `continue` (disabled recipients also land in digests).
 M6 (crit 2 / unknown-recipient branch): change `r is not None and not r.digest_enabled` to `r is None or not r.digest_enabled`.
 M7 (crit 3): MAX_BATCH = 51.
 M8 (crit 3): MAX_BATCH = 49.
 M9 (crit 3): no split — `digests.append((rid, items))` once per recipient instead of the range loop.
 M10 (crit 3): off-by-one slice `items[i:i + MAX_BATCH - 1]`.
 M11 (crit 3): sort/reverse items within a batch (`items[i:i + MAX_BATCH][::-1]`).

Rules: do not edit tests. Do not commit. When finished, ensure `git status --short` in the worktree prints nothing (restore the source; delete any __pycache__ dirs with `find <worktree> -name __pycache__ -type d -prune -exec rm -rf {} +`). Run `git diff --stat` to confirm nothing changed.

Return ONLY a compact table: mutation id | criterion | red test name(s) or SURVIVED. Then one line with final `git status --short` output (should be empty)."}
